messages.content: What is the freezing point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the freezing point of water drops well below 0 °C.  
From the water phase diagram (or from the Clausius–Clapeyron extrapolation of the solid–liquid equilibrium line) the solid–liquid boundary at 10 kPa lies at roughly:

**≈ –21 °C**

So, under a pressure of 10 kPa, water will freeze at about –21 °C.
